Alley means a narrow thoroughfare dedicated or used for public passageway up to 20 feet in width, which usually abuts the rear of the premises, or upon which service entrances or buildings abut, and which is not generally used as a thoroughfare by both pedestrians and vehicles, is not used for general traffic, and is not otherwise officially designated as a street; a way which affords a secondary means of access to abutting property.
Buildable area means that portion of any lot which may be used or built upon once the required front, side and rear yard setbacks have been subtracted from the total area.
Building means any structure having a roof and intended for shelter, housing or enclosure of persons, animals or property of any kind.
Building line means a line extended along the foundation of a building from which is measured the distance that a building must be set back to meet the minimum distance from the building line to the front, rear or side property line or in some cases, to the centerline of an adjacent roadway.
Building official means one or more persons, officers or officials or his authorized representative, whom the governing authority has appointed to administer and enforce, individually or collectively, this chapter and any other ordinances or regulations related to land development and land use.
Building site means the ground area of a building or buildings together with all open spaces surrounded by said building or buildings.
Certified document. A survey, sketch, plat, map or other exhibit is said to be certified when a written statement regarding its accuracy or conformity to specified standards is signed by the specified professional engineers, registered surveyor, architect or other legally recognized person.
Density means the number of units or buildings per acre, or the number of people per unit, building, acre or mile, or the quantity of people, structures or units within a specified area.
Developer means any person, firm, corporation, or agent of the foregoing who or which divides for transfer, sale, rent or lease or in any way develops any land deemed to be a subdivision or mobile home park development as herein defined.
Easement means the right or privilege of using another's property, for purposes such as constructing and maintaining sanitary sewers, water mains, electric lines, telephone lines, storm sewers, gas lines, bicycle paths, pedestrian ways, ingress and egress.
Engineer means any person being licensed by the State of Georgia as an engineer capable of determining the correct manner in which to construct roads, streets, highways, water and sewage systems, drainage system, structures or other technical related areas.
Flag lot means a lot with access provided to the bulk of the lot by means of a narrow corridor no greater in width than 1½ the required lot width. No more than one flag lot shall be permitted to front on the same side of the same street every 1,500 feet. All flag lots shall have a minimum street frontage of at least 60 feet.
Floodprone areas means the land that is usually flooded whenever a rise in the water level of a creek, stream, river or other body of water is experienced; that land adjacent to a creek, stream, river channel, canal or other body of water that is designated as a floodplain or floodprone area by a governmental agency.
Lot means the parcel of land shown on a recorded plat or any piece of land described by a legally recorded deed.
Lot area means the total area of the lot, including easements.
Lot, corner, means a lot located at the intersection of two or more streets.
Lot, double frontage, means a lot, other than a corner lot, which has frontage on more than one street.
Lot interior means any lot which is not a corner lot that has frontage only on one street other than an alley.
Lot line, front. In the case of a lot abutting upon only one street, the front lot line is the line separating such lot from such street. In the case of a corner lot, that part of the lot having the narrowest frontage on any street shall be considered the front lot line. In the case of any other lot, one such line shall be elected to be the front lot line for the purpose of this chapter; provided it is so designated by the Final Development Plan which meets the approval of the governing authority or its authorized representative.
Lot line, rear. The rear lot line is that boundary which is opposite and most distant from the front lot line. In the case of a lot pointed at the rear, or any odd-shaped lot, the rear lot line shall be determined by the governing authority or its authorized representative.
Lot line, side. A side lot line is any lot boundary line not a front lot line or a rear lot line. A side lot line separating a lot from a street is an exterior side lot line. A side lot line separating a lot from a street is an exterior side lot line. A side lot line separating a lot from another lot, or lots, is an interior side lot line.
Lot, reverse frontage, means a lot having frontage on two or more public streets, the access of which is restricted to one street.
Metes and bounds description means a method of property description whereby properties are described by means of their direction and distances from an easily identifiable location or point.
Mobile home (manufactured home) means a dwelling unit fabricated in an off-site facility for installation or assembly at the building site, bearing a label certifying it is constructed in compliance with the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, as amended, USC 5401 et seq. (the HUD Code, which became effective on June 15, 1976); and meeting the following development standards: Structure, when in the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet and which is built on a chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling when connected to the required utilities and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning system contained therein. The square footage shall be calculated using the width and length dimensions noted on the manufactured home's title or bill of sale.
Mobile home park (manufactured home park) means a parcel of land developed for subsequent rental, lease, or residential use for placement of two or more mobile/manufactured homes. All mobile/manufactured homes located within a mobile/manufactured home park must be installed in accordance with the Montgomery County Manufactured Home Ordinance, and all mobile/manufactured home parks shall be designed in accordance with the applicable provisions of this chapter. A mobile/manufactured home occupied by an immediate family member of a property owner shall not be considered for purposes of determining whether a mobile/manufactured home park exists, providing the number of mobile/manufactured home the property owner submits to the governing authority or its designee a mobile home family purpose affidavit confirming the proposed occupant's status as an immediate family member along with a plat of the lot location indicating thereon review and approval by the Montgomery County Health Department confirming the availability of land area sufficient to meet the minimum lot size requirements set forth hereunder. If the mobile/manufactured home ceases to be occupied by an immediate family member, the mobile home/manufactured home shall then be considered the same as any other mobile/manufactured home for purposes of determining whether a mobile/manufactured home park exists. For purposes of this provision, the term "immediate family member" means a child, grandchild, parent, grandparent, sibling or step-child. A mobile home family purpose affidavit may be obtained at the Board of Commissioner's Office.
Nonconforming means a building or other structure, use or lot, which by reason of design, size or use does not conform to the requirements of this chapter.
Plat means a map, plan or layout of a county, city, town, section, subdivision or mobile home park indicating the location and boundaries of properties prepared and stamped by a registered surveyor.
Principal building means the building on a lot in which the principal use of the lot is conducted.
Public use means use of any land, water, buildings by a municipality, public body or board, commission or authority, County, State or Federal government, or any agency thereof for a public service or purpose.
Reserve strip means a strip of land adjacent to a public street or similar right-of-way which has been reserved for the purpose of controlling access to the public way.
Right-of-way line means the boundary of a strip of land designed, reserved, dedicated, or purchased for the purpose of pedestrian or vehicular access.
Setback means the minimum horizontal distance between the right-of-way line, rear or side lines of the lot and the front, rear or side lines of the building. When two adjoining lots under the same ownership are used, the exterior property lines of the lots so grouped shall be used in determining setbacks.
Site means an area designated as a separate and distinct parcel of land on a legally recorded development plan, subdivision plat, or in a legally recorded deed.
Street means a right-of-way affording primary access to abutting property. For the purposes of these regulations, the term "street" shall also mean avenues, boulevards, roads, lanes and other public or private ways.
Street, arterial, means a street of exceptional continuity that is intended to carry the greater portion of through-traffic from one area of the County to another.
Street, collector, means those streets which are neither local streets nor arterial streets. Their location and design are such that they are of exceptional continuity, serve as routes passing through residential areas, and serve as means of moving traffic from local streets and feeding it into arterial streets.
Street, cul-de-sac, means a short local street having but one end open for vehicular traffic, the opposite end being terminated with a permanent turnaround.
Street, dead-end, means a street not intersecting other streets at both ends, and distinguished from a cul-de-sac by not being terminated by a vehicular turnaround.
Street, local, means streets which provide only access to adjacent properties and by nature of their layout serve only vehicles with either origin or destination within the area.
Street, marginal access, means a minor service street which parallels and which is immediately adjacent to an arterial street (frontage road).
Surveyor means a person who is licensed by the State of Georgia as a registered land surveyor.
Structure means anything constructed or erected that requires a fixed location on the ground or which is attached to something having a fixed location on the ground.
Subdivision means the division of a lot of record (which exists at the time of the effective date of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived) into two or more lots, building sites, mobile home sites (manufactured home sites), or other divisions, for the purpose of auction, sale, devise or development, whether immediately or in the future; except that a subdivision does not include the following where the resultant lots are equal to the standards of the governing authority:
(1) The combination or recombination of portions of previously platted lots where the total number of lots is not increased.
(2) A division of property previously held in joint ownership among the joint owners thereof shall not be considered a subdivision for purposes of this chapter.
(3) The transfer of property or any portion thereof from one contiguous owner to another contiguous owner shall not be considered a subdivision for purposes of this chapter.
(4) A single transfer of an interest in property by a landowner shall not be considered a subdivision for purposes of this chapter. However, any subsequent transfers of less than the entire remaining tract of property or subsequent transfer of a portion of the previously transferred property by the owners thereof, their heirs, assigns, or devisees or successors in interest shall be deemed to create a subdivision and the second transfer and all subsequent transfers shall be governed by the terms of this chapter. The utilization of this single transfer exception by a landowner shall not preclude the subsequent use of other allowed subdivision exceptions of subsections (1), (2), (3), (5), (6), and (7) of this definition.
(5) The division of land into parcels of five acres or more where only an existing city, County, or State maintained street is involved and no new streets. (See flag lot which sets forth the requirements for flag lots.)
(6) The division of land into parcels for the purposes of conveying the land directly to an immediate family member. For purposes of this provision, the term "immediate family member" means a child, grandchild, parent, grandparent, sibling or step-child. To obtain a review of a plat being submitted under this exception, a family purpose affidavit must be submitted by the grantor to the governing authority or its designee certifying the status of the grantee as an immediate family member. A family purpose affidavit may be obtained at the Board of Commissioner's Office.
(7) A transfer of a security interest in property by a landowner for purposes of obtaining financing from a financial institution where ownership remains the same provided the lot fronts on a city, County or State maintained street and complies with the lot size requirements set forth in section 26-26.
Use means any purpose for which a building or tract of land may be designed, arranged, maintained, or occupied; or any activity, occupation, business, or operation carried on in a building or structure or on a tract of land.
Waterfront. Any site shall be considered as waterfront property provided any or all of its lot lines abut on or are contiguous to any body of water, including a creek, canal, river or any other body of water, natural or artificial, including marshland, not including a swimming pool, whether said lot line is front, rear or side.
Yard means a required open space on a lot that is left unoccupied with structures and facilities, except as permitted in this chapter. A yard may also be known as a setback.
Yard, front, means the open space on a lot located between the right-of-way boundary of the abutting street and the front building line as extended to the lot lines to either side. Any yard lying between an abutting street and the building line is considered a front yard.
Yard, rear, means the open space located between the rear property line and the rear building line as extended to the side lot lines.
Yard, side, means the open space located between the side property line and the side building line as extended to the front and rear lot lines.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 5.2)
435:
(a) In order to create, develop, construct, alter, expand or sell lots within a subdivision or mobile home park, a developer must first secure approval of a Final Development Plan from the governing authority. The procedure for review, consideration, and approval of a Development Plan consists of two separate steps. These are:
(1) Review of Sketch Plan by the governing authority.
(2) Review of Final Development Plan by the governing authority.
(b) It is recommended that developers considering subdivision or mobile home park development seek a predevelopment review by the Montgomery County Health Department prior to beginning work on their development plan.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 6.1)
436:
A Final Development Plan shall not be submitted for review until the developer or his agent has obtained review and approval from the following:
(1) The Montgomery County Health Department shall review the water supply and sewage disposal facilities to be provided on all development plans after being provided with such percolation tests or other information as it may require. In addition, it shall make determinations in all matters concerning the public health, as specified herein. Such determinations and recommendations shall be in writing and accompany the Final Development Plan. Regardless of individual lot sizes within a development, a developer shall be required to provide the Health Department with a soil map and soil descriptions based on high intensity soil study conducted in compliance with the Department of Human Resources' current Manual for On-Site Sewage Management Systems. Prior to granting approval of a Final Development Plan, the Montgomery County Health Department shall confirm the availability of land area sufficient to meet the minimum lot size requirements set forth in section 26-26.
(2) The Chairperson of the Board of Commissioners or his authorized designee shall review the Final Development Plan for conformity of its proposed streets with adopted design standards and existing and proposed public street improvements.
(3) A land disturbing activity permit, pursuant to the Georgia Erosion and Sedimentation Act of 1975, including all amendments in effect as of the date of the application for such permit, shall be required prior to any land disturbing activity on the project site. "Land disturbing activity" includes, but is not limited to, clearing, dredging, grading, excavating, transporting and filling of land. An approved sediment and erosion control plan and review by the soil conservation service is required as part of the application for the land disturbing activity permit. The permit must include a Wetlands Survey Clearance Affidavit and Floodplain Map/Affidavit, prepared by a licensed professional engineer or land surveyor.
(4) If the proposed subdivision or mobile home park development includes or abuts any part of the State highway system, the developer shall submit the Development Plan to the Department of Transportation for review and approval in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 32-6-151.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 6.2)
437:
(a) Application for Sketch Plan review. The developer shall submit to the governing authority, at least 25 days prior to the next regularly scheduled monthly meeting of the governing authority, the following:
(1) A letter requesting Sketch Plan review and giving the name and address and phone number of a person to whom the notice of the hearing by the governing authority on the Sketch Plan shall be sent/called.
(2) Eight copies of the Sketch Plan. Additional copies of the Sketch Plan may be requested by the governing authority.
(3) Sketch Plan application fee, as set forth in the Montgomery County Schedule of Fees, shall accompany the Sketch Plan. Said fee is non-returnable.
(b) Review of Sketch Plan. No Sketch Plan shall be acted upon by the governing authority without affording a hearing thereon. The purpose of the Sketch Plan is to assist the developer prior to extensive site planning necessary for the preparation of the preliminary plat and to enable the developer to become familiar with the regulations affecting the land to be subdivided. The governing authority shall review and approve, disapprove, or approve with modification the Sketch Plan. Pertinent comments and recommendations shall be noted in the minutes of the governing authority.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 6.3)
438:
(a) Application for Final Development Plan review. The developer must submit to the governing authority, at least 25 days prior to the next regularly scheduled monthly meeting of the governing authority, the following:
(1) A letter requesting review and approval of the Final Development Plan and giving the name and address of a person to whom the notice of the hearing by the governing authority on the Final Development Plan shall be sent.
(2) The original and five copies of the Final Development Plan.
(3) If streets are to be built, the developer will indicate such developer's proposal for a bond or bank letter of credit to assure their proper and timely construction.
(4) Final Development Plan application fee as set forth in the Montgomery County Schedule of Fees shall accompany the Final Development Plan. Said fee is non-returnable.
(b) Review of Final Development Plan.
(1) The Chairperson of the Board of Commissioners, or other person or persons designated by the Chairperson, shall check the Final Development Plan for conformance with the rules and regulations of this chapter and report his findings to the governing authority, which shall afford a hearing on the Final Development Plan, notice of the time and place of which shall be sent by the governing authority by registered or certified mail to the person designated in the letter requesting Final Development Plan review and approval.
(2) Thereafter, the governing authority shall approve or disapprove the Final Development Plan. A notation of the action shall be made on both the original and one copy of the Final Development Plan. The original shall be returned to the developer or his agent. Upon approval being stamped thereon, a developer shall proceed within 15 days from the date of approval to record the Final Development Plan in the Clerk's Office of the Montgomery County Superior Court.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 6.4)
439:
In the event the developer plans to secure approval of the Development Plan design by the Federal Housing Administration, it is required that such approval be secured prior to submission of the Preliminary Development Plan to the governing authority.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 6.4)
440:
No portion of a subdivision or mobile home park development shall be approved which is subject to inundation by a flood of 100 years frequency or less, and to all State and Federal laws and regulations. All subdivision and mobile home park developments must be designed to minimize flood damage; all public utilities and facilities, such as sewer, gas, electrical and water systems, shall be located, elevated and constructed to minimize or eliminate flood damage; adequate drainage must be provided to reduce exposure to flood hazards; water supply systems and/or sanitary sewage systems must be designed to minimize or eliminate flood damage; adequate drainage must be provided to eliminate exposure to flood hazards; water supply systems and/or sanitary sewage systems must be designed to minimize infiltration of floodwaters into the system and discharges from the system into floodwaters; and on-site sewage management systems must be located so as to avoid impairment of them or contamination from them during flooding.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 6.5)
444:
The Final Development Plan shall be drawn so that the overall dimensions of the plat do not exceed 18 inches by 22 inches. If the Final Development Plan is drawn in two or more sections, each section shall be accompanied by a key map showing the location of the several sections. The Final Development Plan shall also contain the following specific information:
(1) Name of owner of record.
(2) Name of subdivision or mobile home park development, data, north arrow, and graphic scale.
(3) Name, registration number, and seal of registered land surveyor.
(4) Names of counties in which development is located and location map.
(5) Sufficient data to determine readily and reproduce accurately on the ground the location, bearing, length and width of every street and alley line, lot line, easement, boundary line and building line, whether curved or straight. This shall include radius, point of tangency, and other data for curved property lines and curved streets, to an appropriate accuracy and in conformance with good surveying practice.
(6) Name of owners of record of all adjoining land and all property boundaries, watercourses, streets, easements, utilities and other such improvements, which cross or form any boundary line of the tract being subdivided.
(7) Exact boundaries of original property lines within the tract of land being developed shown with bearing and distances.
(8) Streets and alleys, right-of-way, and street names, including street profiles reflecting grades and positive drainage, and roadway typical sections.
(9) Rights-of-way of easements; location, widths, and purposes, including storm drainage easements.
(10) Lot lines, minimum building setback lines, street trees and lot and block numbers.
(11) Parks, or other public open spaces, if any.
(12) All dimensions shall be to the nearest 1/100 of a foot and angles to the nearest second.
(13) Accurate description of the location of all monuments and markers.
(14) Utility easements by width and location.
(15) Drainage design, including sketches of drainage areas, pipe/culvert sizes required, invert elevations, etc., prepared and stamped by a professional engineer.
(16) Any additional information not covered by subsections (1) through (15) of this section which is required to be included on a Sketch Plan. (See section 26-60.)
(17) Copy of subdivision covenants, if any.
(18) The following signed certificates shall appear on the Final Development Plan which is submitted to the governing authority by the developer:

(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 7.2)
445:
Upon obtaining approval of the Final Development Plan, all of the development's permanent reference points shall be placed in accordance with the following requirements:
(1) Corner tie. At least one corner of the subdivision or mobile home park development shall be designated by course and distance (tie) from a readily discernible reference marker. If a corner is within 2,000 feet of a U.S. Coast and Geodetic Station, U.S. Geological Survey, or Georgia Grid System coordinated monument, then this corner shall be marked with a monument so designated by computed X and Y coordinates which shall appear on the map with a statement identifying this station or monument to an accuracy of 1:10,000. When such a monument or station is not available, the tie shall be made to some permanent and readily recognizable landmark or identifiable point, physical object or structure. In subdivision or mobile home park developments of more than ten lots, the information for this corner tie shall include elevation above sea level making it in effect a benchmark which can be used to determine if individual lots are in a floodprone area.
(2) Monuments.
a. Monuments shall be located in the ground at all angles in the boundaries of the subdivision or mobile home park development; at the intersection lines of streets and at the intersection of the lines of streets with boundaries of the Final Development Plan and at the intersection of alleys with the boundaries of the subdivision or mobile home park development; at all points of curvature, points in the side lines of streets and alleys; and at all angles of an intermediate traverse line.
b. It is not intended or required that monuments be placed within the traveled portion of a street to mark angles in the boundary of the subdivision or mobile home park development, if the angle points can be readily reestablished by reference to monuments along the side lines of the streets.
c. All required monuments shall be placed flush with the ground where practicable.
d. If the required location of a monument is in an inaccessible place, or where the location of a monument would be clearly impracticable, it is sufficient to place a reference monument nearby and the precise location thereof shall be clearly indicated on the plat and referenced to the true point.
e. All monuments used shall be made of a minimum of solid iron or steel bars at least one-half inch in diameter and 24 inches long.
(3) Control corners. Within each block of a subdivision or mobile home park development at least two monuments designed and designated as control corners shall be installed. All control corners shall be constructed of concrete and shall be at least four inches in diameter or square and not less than three feet in length. Each monument shall have imbedded in its top or attached by a suitable means, a metal plate of noncorrosive materials and marked plainly with the point, the surveyor's registration number, the month and year it was installed and the words "control corner."
(4) Property markers. A steel or wrought iron pipe or the equivalent not less than one-half inch in diameter and at least 24 inches in length shall set all corners, except those located by monuments.
(5) Accuracy. Land surveys shall be at an accuracy of at least 1:10,000.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 7.3)
448:
Subdivision developments shall be subject to the following requirements:
(1) Water supply. All water systems shall be installed in accordance with the rules and regulations of the Montgomery County Health Department, County Board of Health, and the Environmental Protection Division of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources. The water system shall be a permitted community water system as required by the State of Georgia Safe Water Drinking Act.
(2) Sanitary sewage. If a sanitary sewer is installed in a subdivision or mobile home park development, sanitary sewers shall be installed to the plans and specifications approved by and in accordance with the rules and administrative regulations of the Montgomery County Health Department. When the sewer line is located in a street right-of-way and it will be necessary to cut into the street surface to serve the abutting lots, a connection shall be stubbed-out to the property line to serve each lot prior to surfacing the street.
(3) Sewage disposal systems. Prior to the construction of any sewage disposal system, such as private septic tanks, an oxidation pond or other facility, the location, size, plans and specifications of such a facility shall be approved by and be in accordance with the rules and administrative regulations of the governing authority and the Montgomery County Health Department.
(4) Curb and gutters. If concrete curbs or paved valley type gutters are required, they shall be installed in accordance with plans and specifications prepared by an engineer, registered surveyor, or architect, and approved by the governing authority or its designee.
(5) Street grading and surfacing. It shall be the developer's responsibility to construct streets in developments governed by this chapter. Street grading, base preparation, and surfacing of all streets shall be carried out by the developer according to the plans and specifications approved by the Chairperson of the Board of Commissioners or his authorized designee and the Georgia Department of Transportation as required. This requirement shall not apply to existing County or State maintained streets. (See section 26-106 for street design standards.)
(6) Storm drainage. An adequate drainage system, including necessary open ditches, pipes, culverts, storm sewers, intersectional drains, drop inlets, bridges and other necessary appurtenances, shall be designed by and installed according to the plans and specifications approved by a registered engineer. All storm drainage pipe shall be concrete or galvanized corrugated metal, with a minimum diameter of 18 inches.
(7) Street name signs. Street name signs shall be installed at all intersections within a subdivision or mobile home park development. The location and design shall be approved by the governing authority or its designee, and coordinated with local 911 authority.
(8) Development entrances. The governing authority may limit the number of entrances, driveways, or "curb cuts." Design standards on County or State streets and roads shall be consistent with all State, Federal, and local laws and applicable ordinances, including the Georgia Department of Transportation Rules and all amendments or revisions in effect as of the date of the Final Development Plan approval. The governing authority may consider safety as well as require available alternatives for reducing the number of entrances, driveways, or "curb cuts."
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 8.1)
449:
If it should become necessary to revise an approved Final Development Plan due to dimensional error, a revised Final Development Plan shall be submitted to the Clerk of Court for final recording after the governing authority has approved and signed the revised Final Development Plan.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 8.2)
450:
To ensure installation and completion of required improvements approved by the governing authority as part of a Final Development Plan, the governing authority or its designee may require a bond or bank letter of credit, in an amount and with a surety or bank and containing conditions and terms satisfactory to it, providing for and securing to the County a period specified by the governing authority or its designee and expressed in the bond or bank letter of credit; and the County is hereby granted the power to enforce such bonds or bank letters of credit by all legal and equitable remedies. The form of the performance bond or bank letter of credit is subject to approval by the governing authority or its designee.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 8.3)
451:
The County shall not accept title to or assume responsibility for maintaining any street until at least one year after the street has been constructed and paved in accordance with this chapter. Prior to acceptance, the governing authority will inspect the roads to ensure compliance with this chapter. Fee for inspection will be in accordance with the County Schedule of Fees.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 8.4)
452:
The governing authority shall not approve a subdivision development in a location where the existing road sand streets providing primary access are inadequate to serve the additional traffic generated by the development. If the ditches on existing County roads or streets are to be used for drainage from the subdivision development, the developer will re-grade said ditches and provide an all-weather drainage outlet. All re-grading and drainage outlets shall be approved by the governing authority or its authorized representatives.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 8.5)
455:
(a) Generally. Streets shall conform to the current DOT and/or County road construction and maintenance specifications in effect at the time of the development application and may differ from those requirements outlined in this chapter. If the DOT and County road construction maintenance specifications are different, the more stringent specifications shall apply.
(1) Subgrade shall be compacted to 100 percent of the laboratory maximum dry density.
(2) Graded aggregate base should meet section 310 of the Georgia DOT specifications and be no less than four inches in depth. It shall be compacted to 100 percent of the maximum dry density.
(3) Any pertinent laboratory testing, to verify the above items, shall be done for every 1,000 square yards of material placed.
(4) All slopes both cut and filled shall have a maximum 3:1 slope; all drainage ditches shall have a minimum depth of two feet.
(b) Conformity to existing maps or plans. The location and width of all proposed streets shall (if applicable) be in conformity with official plans and maps and with existing amended plans of the governing authority.
(c) Continuation of adjoining street system. The proposed street layout shall be coordinated with the street system of the surrounding area. Where possible, existing major streets shall be extended.
(d) Access to adjacent properties. Where it is desirable to provide for street access to adjoining property, proposed streets shall be extended by dedication to the boundary of such property and a temporary turnaround shall be provided. Houses fronting on minor streets shall have access from minor streets only.
(e) Street names. Proposed streets, which are obviously in alignment with other existing and named streets, shall bear the assigned name of the existing streets. In no case shall the name of the proposed streets duplicate or be phonetically similar to existing street names, irrespective of the use of suffix, street, avenue, boulevard, drive, place, court, etc. It shall be unlawful for any person in laying out any new street or road to name such street or road on any plat or Final Development Plan, by marking or in any deed or instrument, without first obtaining approval of the governing authority or its designee.
(f) Minor streets. Minor streets shall be so laid out that their use by through-traffic will be discouraged.
(g) Trees. It is recommended that as many trees as possible remain on the site during the initial clearing and grading and that trees normally remain unless they lie within a planned public right-of-way, within a planned building site or within the necessary paved areas surrounding or adjacent to the primary structure.
(h) Railroads and highways (freeways, expressways). Railroad rights-of-way and limited access highways where so located as to affect the development of adjoining lands shall be treated as follows:

456:
Easements having a minimum width of ten feet and locate along the front, side or rear lot lines shall be provided as required for utility lines and underground mains and cables.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 9.2)
457:
If crosswalks are required by the governing authority they shall not be less than ten feet wide where it is deemed essential in order to provide circulation or access to schools, playgrounds, shopping centers, transportation or other community facilities.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 9.3)
458:
(a) Setback lines. No dwelling shall be located within 40 feet of its front lot line or any street right-of-way, 15 feet of any side lot line or 25 feet of any rear lot line.
(b) Lot size with private water and private sewer.
(1) Minimum area: Subdivision lots served by both an individual well and an individual septic tank shall contain a minimum lot area of at least 43,560 square feet for a single housing unit unless the Montgomery County Health Officer determines that 43,560 square feet is not sufficient.
(2) Minimum width: 200 feet between side lot lines measured at the front setback line.
(3) Minimum depth: 200 feet.
(c) Lot size with public water and individual septic tank.
(1) Minimum area: Subdivision lots served by community or public water and individual septic tanks shall contain the minimum lot area of at least 22,000 square feet for a single housing unit unless the Montgomery County Health Officer determines that 22,000 square feet is not sufficient.
(2) Minimum width: 100 feet between side lot lines measured at the front setback line.
(3) Minimum depth: 200 feet.
(d) Lot size with public water and public sewer.
(1) Minimum area: Subdivision lots served by community or public water and sewer shall contain the minimum to area of at least 22,000 square feet for a single housing unit unless the Montgomery County Health Officer determines that 22,000 square feet is not sufficient.
(2) Minimum width: 100 feet between side lot lines measured at the front setback line.
(3) Minimum depth: 150 feet.
(e) Orientation of lot lines. Side lot lines shall be as nearly at right angles as possible to street lines.
(f) Lot location. Each lot shall abut upon a dedicated public street on which it has access.
(g) Additional requirements. No mobile home shall be admitted to any subdivision unless it can be demonstrated that the mobile home meets the requirements of the Montgomery County Manufactured Home Ordinance.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 9.4)
459:
(a) Development size. Each mobile home park development shall have a minimum area of not less than ten acres.
(b) Setbacks. No mobile home or other building within a mobile home park shall be located within 25 feet of its front lot line or any street right-of-way; ten feet of any side lot line or any rear lot line.
(c) Lot size. Mobile home lot sites shall have a lot area as required in subsection (d), (e) or (f) of this section with a minimum lot width of 100 feet unless more stringent lot size requirements are required by the Montgomery County Health Officer to conform to State health regulations. In cul-de-sacs, the width of the mobile home space shall be at least 100 feet at the location of the center of the mobile home unit.
(d) Lot size with public water and individual septic tank. Mobile home lots served by community or public water and individual septic tanks shall contain the minimum lot area of 12,500 square feet unless the County Health Officer determines that 12,500 square feet is not sufficient.
(e) Lot size with public water and public sewer. Mobile home lots served by community or public water and sewer shall contain the minimum lot area of 12,500 square feet unless the County Health Officer determines that 12,500 square feet is not sufficient.
(f) Lot size with private water and private sewer. Mobile home lots served by both an individual well and an individual septic tank shall contain a minimum lot area of at least 43,560 square feet unless the County Health Officer determines that 43,560 square feet is not sufficient.
(g) Orientation of lot lines. Side lot lines shall be as nearly at right angles as possible to street lines.
(h) Lot location. All mobile home lots must abut upon an interior street (a street located completely inside the boundaries of a mobile home park), which has direct access to a street outside the park. Each mobile home sites shall be provided with a driveway connecting with this interior street and sufficient to provide two off-street parking spaces. No mobile home site within a mobile home park shall have immediate access to a street located outside the boundaries of the mobile home park.
(i) Buffer. A buffer strip of at least 75 feet wide shall be located adjacent to each exterior property line of the mobile home park and shall not be included within any individual mobile home lot. This buffer strip shall be increased to a width of 125 feet when located adjacent to existing residential, commercial or industrial development. An area of sufficient width to hide the view of the mobile home park development shall be densely planted along the exterior of the buffer zone with fast growing evergreen shrubs or trees. This strip shall be part of the Final Development Plan and shall be so designated on the plan: "This strip is reserved for the planting of trees and shrubs by the owner. The placement of structures hereon is prohibited."
(j) Recreation. Where the average lot sizes for a mobile home park development are less than 22,000 square feet, a minimum of ten percent of the total area of any mobile home park shall be set aside and designed for recreational purposes.
(k) Additional requirements. No mobile home shall be admitted to any mobile home park unless it can be demonstrated that the mobile home meets the requirements of the Montgomery County Manufactured Home Ordinance.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 9.5)
460:
(a) Soils. The governing authority shall not approve a development where the soil conditions have been determined not suitable for development by the County Health Department pursuant to local, State, and Federal laws, regulations and standards.
(b) Health, safety, and welfare. In approving a Final Development Plan, the governing authority may attach additional conditions to protect the health, safety and welfare of both the occupants of the subdivision and the occupants of the surrounding property.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 9.6)
463:
When, due to unnecessary or undue hardship experienced by the developer of a tract of land it is impractical for a developer to comply with the interpretations of the design requirements of this chapter, the governing authority shall be authorized to vary such requirements provided the intent and purpose of this chapter is not violated. The fact that a financial hardship will be suffered if a variance is not granted is of itself insufficient grounds for granting a variance. Such variations, and the reasons for granting them, shall be entered into the minutes of the governing authority.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 10.1)
466:
(a) Submission for filing.
(1) No plat, deed, or other document or instrument describing a subdivision or mobile home park, including those exceptions as enumerated under the definition of "subdivision" in section 26-6 shall be submitted for filing or recording in the Office of the Clerk of Court of Montgomery County unless it shall have the approval of the governing authority or its designee inscribed thereon.
(2) No plat of a resurvey of an existing parcel of land containing no division of said existing parcel shall be submitted for filing or recording in the Office of the Clerk of Court of Montgomery County unless it shall have the approval of the governing authority or its designee inscribed thereon.
(b) Requirements for section 26-26 approval. To obtain the approval required under section 26-26, the registered surveyor and/or an attorney shall provide a statement on the plat, deed, or other document or instrument certifying the applicable exception, as enumerated in the definition of "subdivision" in section 26-6, being utilized or that the plat is a resurvey of an existing parcel of land containing no division of said existing parcel. The statement shall be in substantially the following form:
"I (name of registered surveyor/attorney), hereby certify that this (plat, deed, or other document or instrument describing property by means of a legal description) meets the following exception under the Montgomery County Subdivision Ordinance: (describe exception, as enumerated in the definition of "subdivision" in section 26-6)."
(c) Examples of descriptions of exceptions, as enumerated in the definition of "subdivision" in section 26-6.
(1) This (plat, deed or other document or instrument describing property by means of a legal description) represents a division of property previously held in joint ownership among the following joint owners: (name owners);
(2) This (plat, deed or other document or instrument describing property by means of a legal description) represents the transfer of property from one contiguous owner (name owner) to another contiguous owner (name owner); and
(3) This (plat, deed or other document or instrument describing property by means of a legal description) represents a single transfer of an interest in property by a landowner (name landowner). To the best of my knowledge and belief, the parcel to be transferred is not a portion of a lot of record created on or after the date of execution of the Montgomery County Subdivision Ordinance.
(d) Review fee. An applicant for review of a plat, deed, or other document or instrument as required by section 26-82(1) must pay a review fee as set forth in the County Schedule of Fees.
(e) Acceptance for filing. The Office of the Clerk of Court the County shall not accept, file, or record any plat, deed, or other document or instrument requiring approval under section 26-8(1) without approval being entered thereon by the governing authority or its designee.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 11.1)
467:
No lot, street, alley, improvement, easement, right-of-way or other property or property right of any kind shall be conveyed, by deed or otherwise, to the County, the governing authority or other public authority without its express acceptance of such conveyance as indicated by the signature of its authorized agent on such deed or other document of conveyance.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 11.2)
468:
(a) Sale, transfer, or lease. No lot or parcel of land shall be sold, transferred, or leased until the Final Development Plan, of which said lot or parcel is a part, shall have been approved as provided for in this chapter.
(b) Construction standards. A building or structure shall be considered substandard if or when it does not meet the requirements of the Uniform Building Code of Georgia, or any other Code or ordinance adopted by the County or its governing authority.
(c) Occupancy. For any subdivision or mobile home park development subject to the provisions of this chapter, no building or structure may be occupied for dwelling or other purposes, nor shall an occupancy permit be issued, if required, for any building or structure until all streets and required utility installations, including water supply and sanitary sewer systems, have been completed.
(d) Erection and location of buildings. Any building or structure erected or located in violation of this chapter shall be deemed an unlawful structure, and the governing authority or its designated official(s) may bring appropriate action to enjoin such erection or cause it to be vacated or removed.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 11.3)
469:
The lease of, transfer of, sale of, agreement to sell, or negotiation to sell or lease lots by reference to an exhibition of, or other use of a plat or plan of a subdivision or mobile home park development subject to the requirements of this chapter that has not been given approval by the governing authority is prohibited, and the description by metes and bounds in the instrument of transfer or lease shall not exempt the transaction from such penalties. The County may enjoin such lease, transfer or sale or agreement by appropriate action.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 11.4)
470:
The creation, development, construction, alteration, or expansion of a subdivision by a developer without first obtaining approval of a Final Development Plan from the governing authority is prohibited and shall be a violation of this chapter.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 11.5)
471:
It shall be unlawful for a person in laying out any new street or road to name such street or road on any plat, by any marking or in any deed or instrument without first obtaining the approval of the governing authority.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 11.6)
472:
A lawful use of or vested right to use any building, structure or land existing at the time of the adoption of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived or the adoption of any amendment thereto may be continued subject to the restrictions contained in this chapter even though such use does not conform with the regulations of this chapter except that:
(1) A nonconforming use or structure shall not be changed to another nonconforming use;
(2) A nonconforming use or structure shall not be extended or enlarged beyond the area of use or the size of the structure as it existed on the date of the adoption of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived or the adoption of any amendments thereto.
(3) A nonconforming use or structure shall not be re-established after discontinuance for six months regardless of any reservation of an intent not to abandon.
(4) Any intended nonconforming use for which a vested right was acquired prior to the adoption of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived or the adoption of an amendment thereto shall be prohibited unless such intended nonconforming use for which a vested right was acquired is actually commenced within one year of the adoption of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived or the adoption of an amendment thereto regardless of the intent or expectation to commence or abandon such nonconforming use.
(5) A nonconforming use or structure shall not be rebuilt, altered, or repaired except as provided herein:
a. If the structure is altered or repaired, said alterations or repairs shall be in conformity with the building codes in force at the time of said alteration or repair; provided, however, that said alteration or repair shall not extend or enlarge the structure being altered or repaired;
b. If the structure is totally rebuilt, the replacement structure shall conform with all the requirements of this chapter, except as to the district; provided, however, said replacement structure may not occupy an area greater than the replaced structure.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 11.7)
475:
A violation of this chapter shall be a misdemeanor offense and shall be punished by a fine not to exceed $1,000.00 and/or imprisonment of not more than 12 months. After any developer, person, or entity has been notified by the governing authority or its designee that such person or entity is in violation of this chapter, each day of continued violation shall constitute a separate offense punishable by like fine. In addition to or in lieu of the foregoing the governing authority may, whether by legal process or otherwise, seek to enjoin, correct, and/or abate any violations of this chapter.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 12.1)
476:
If the governing authority determines that certain improvements to a subdivision do not comply with the approved Final Development Plan or any other provisions of this chapter, the developer or owner shall be deemed in violation of this chapter, and upon demand by the Board of Commissioners, shall immediately correct any deficiencies as required by the governing authority
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 12.2)
479:
The regulations expressed in this chapter shall be considered as the minimum provisions for the protection of the health, safety, economy, good order, appearance, convenience and welfare of the general public.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 13.1)
480:
Whenever the requirements made under authority of this chapter impose higher standards than are required in any other statute or local ordinance or regulation, provisions of this chapter shall govern.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 13.2)
481:
Should any section or provision of this chapter be declared by the courts to be unconstitutional or invalid, such a declaration shall not affect the chapter as a whole, or any other part thereof other than the part so declared to be unconstitutional or invalid.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 13.3)
482:
All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict with and less restrictive than any of the provisions of this chapter are hereby repealed.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 13.4)
483:
These regulations shall not be construed as abating any action now pending under, or by virtue of, prior existing subdivision regulations, or as discontinuing, abating, modifying, or altering any penalty accruing or about to accrue, or as affecting the liability of any person, firm, or corporation, or as waiving any right of the County under any section or provision existing at the time of adoption of these regulations, or as vacating or annulling any rights obtained by any person, firm, or corporation, by lawful action of the County or its governing authority except as shall be expressly provided for in these regulations.
(Ord. of 8-2-2005(2), § 13.5)

486:
[(a) Membership.] Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-5-290 there is an established Montgomery County Board of Tax Assessors. The Board of Tax Assessors shall consist of not less than three nor more than five members to be appointed by the Montgomery County Board of Commissioners. The appointment up to a five member board is authorized but not mandated.
Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-5-292 the Montgomery County Chief Appraiser is eligible to serve on the Board of Tax Assessors if authorized in a meeting of the Board of Commissioners.
[(b) Compensation.] Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-5-294 each member of the Board of Tax Assessors shall be paid as compensation for his services an amount to be determined from time to time by the Board of Commissioners. The compensation to be paid to a member of the Board of Tax Assessors shall not be less than $20.00 per day for the time he is actually discharging the duties required of him. Attendance at required approved appraisal courses shall be part of the official duties of a member of the Board of Tax Assessors and he shall be paid for each day in attendance at such courses and shall be allowed reasonable expenses necessarily incurred in connection with the courses. The compensation of the members of the Board of Tax Assessors and other expenses as may necessarily be incurred in the performance of the duties of the Board shall be paid from the county treasury in the same manner as other payments by the County are made.
[(c) Term.] Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-5-295 appointment of members to the Board of Tax Assessors will be for a term of six years and until a successor is duly appointed and qualified.
[(d) Certification of appointment.] Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-5-290(c) the order making an appointment to the Board of Tax Assessors shall be regularly entered upon the record of the Superior Court of Montgomery County. A certificate from the Clerk of the Superior Court reciting the order and stating that the person appointed has taken the oath required by law shall constitute the commission of a member. No other commission shall be required. The Clerk of the Superior Court shall transmit a copy of the certificate to the State Revenue Commissioner within five days of the date the oath is administered.
(Res. No. 16-08-04, 8-8-2016)
